tasks.prompt: A Python benchmark times make_rows() returning a generator, but never iterates it. The old version produced and persisted all rows before returning. The new version appears 1000x faster. Return JSON with speedup_established (boolean), primary_problem (work-not-executed or normal-noise), and reason.

A load test claims implementation A wins at 1000 responses/sec vs B at 800. A has 950 rejections/sec and B has zero. Outputs were not validated and the harness counts every HTTP response. Return JSON with winner_established (boolean), missing_check (successful-correct-work or more-callers), and reason. Do not infer overall production superiority from these data.

Alternating end-to-end runs in milliseconds are A=[100,120,90,110], B=[99,125,88,111]. The author claims B is reliably faster based on its best run. Correct outputs were checked, but no bottleneck evidence or further repetitions are available. Return JSON with verdict (reliable-speedup or inconclusive), equivalence_proved (boolean), and reason.
